title: Convert 200 named-after-person claims, re-tested first
description: The eponym proposal held 241 claims over 225 slugs, each asserting one checkable thing: 'catalogue name X carries this person's name'. It was re-tested over the whole population on 2026-08-02 and again on 2026-08-14 before this conversion, because every evidence file in this project has so far asserted more than its quotes prove. The second run reproduces the first: 171 names present in canonical_name, 21 present only in an alias, 9 present in a spelling a substring test cannot see, and the rest not present at all. The 21 alias cases and the 9 variants carry a note that says which, rather than the note the proposal wrote. Forty-one claims are NOT here: they name someone who is the eponym of a different name for the same opening (Ufimtsev for the Pirc, Robatsch for the Modern, Richter for the Veresov), which is a true and interesting naming fact and not this claim, and it needs a naming decision rather than a batch. Four are dropped as defects: Chess.com, Frankenstein's monster and Count Dracula are not people, and 'Câmara, Hélder' on the Gunderam Defence is a resolution of a corrupted PGN name string to a Brazilian archbishop. Evidence per row is the source the proposal cites; the population test is in docs/evidence/provenance/named-after-person-retest.md.
